paper.core_task: Robust distributed gradient descent against adversarial workers.

contributions.name: An adaptive pre-aggregation gradient clipping scheme for robust aggregation
contributions.author_claim_text: We propose ARC, wherein prior to aggregating the gradients, the server clips the largest k := ⌊2(f /n)(n -f )⌋ gradients using a clipping parameter given by the (Euclidean) norm of the (k + 1)-th largest gradient.
contributions.description: A novel adaptive clipping method that automatically adjusts the clipping threshold based on gradient norms and the number of adversarial workers, without requiring prior knowledge of honest gradients.

contributions.name: A preserved robustness guarantee for composed aggregation methods
contributions.author_claim_text: We prove that ARC preserves the robustness guarantee of the original robust aggregation method.
contributions.description: Theoretical proof that pre-composing ARC with any (f, κ)-robust aggregation method results in a composition that is (f, κ + 2f/(n-2f))-robust, preserving convergence guarantees.

contributions.name: An improved learning guarantee under bounded initial gradients
contributions.author_claim_text: We demonstrate that ARC possesses an additional property... Leveraging this property, we show that ARC circumvents the lower bound established under data heterogeneity, provided the honest gradients are bounded at model initialization.
contributions.description: ARC can improve convergence beyond the standard lower bound when model initialization is good, as it constrains the norm of the aggregated output by the largest norm of honest gradients.

novelty_claims.text: The proposed ARC scheme is novel and interesting. It is easy to implement and does not require any additional tuning parameters.
